name: Usuzumi-zakura (Neodani Usuzumi Cherry)
description: The Usuzumi-zakura is a National Natural Monument and one of Japan's Three Great Cherry Trees, standing in Usuzumi Park in Motosu City. This ~1,500-year-old Edo-higan cherry blooms in pale buds that deepen to white and fade to an ink-like shade before falling — the 'light ink' color that gives it its name.
highlights: One of Japan's Three Great Cherry Trees
Blossoms that fade to pale ink
notes: Free to view; the tree stands beside the Itadori River in Usuzumi Park. Best seen late March to early April; the surrounding Motosu area also offers a local railway museum. Access is by car (about 50 min from Gifu City); no direct train service. The tree is said to have been planted by legendary figure Prince Yamatotakeru.
